solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reject ready to join first-rate team

blocks.note: 'ready, steady, go' — set means prepared
an A side is a top team, as in the A team

explanation.surface: A player, finally ready, rejects the chance to join an elite team.
explanation.walkthrough: The team splits as A (first-rate, as in A1) plus SIDE, and the enumeration re-cuts it into a two-word phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard or put something away as not wanted is a phrasal-verb equivalent of throwing out or dismissing it.

clue.text: Revealing book from Kipling — notice covers

indicators.note: whatever covers something else wraps around it, so one piece goes outside another

blocks.note: to spy is to notice or catch sight of
Kim is Kipling's novel about a boy in British India

explanation.surface: A racy book by Kipling hidden under a notice, as if someone were censoring it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' looks like it describes the book, but it is the definition, in the sense of showing a lot of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing described as revealing shows a lot of skin, which is what scanty, barely-there garments do.

clue.text: Spell-check?

blocks.note: surface reading: the software feature that checks spelling
setter's reading: a check or restriction on a spell, i.e. a period of time

explanation.walkthrough: A spell is also a stretch of time (a cold spell), and a check is a curb, so a spell-check is a cap on how long something may last.
explanation.definitionFit: A restriction placed on a period of time is exactly a curb on duration, a deadline or allotted span.

clue.text: Wind like this carrying enormous bird round

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: Latin sic, 'thus', printed after a quotation to mean it is exactly like this
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A gust strong enough to carry a huge bird around the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads as a direction for the bird, but it is just a letter shaped like a ring, added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty Mediterranean wind blowing north from the Sahara.

clue.text: Daughter on break finds meaning

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A daughter on a gap year finding purpose in life.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general gist or sense, as in 'if you catch my drift'.

clue.text: Light reversed in fleeting image

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, spanning the gap between them
turned backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words, read forwards

explanation.surface: A flash of light glimpsed backwards in a brief picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Read fleETING Image from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or fuse is to set it burning, the verb sense of kindle.

clue.text: Girl out with men shows mischievous spirit

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman on a night out with the lads reveals her impish side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like a night on the town, but it scrambles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for unexplained faults in machinery, a small troublemaking sprite.

clue.text: Opener enthusiastic about collecting runs

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece gathers another inside

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A keen opening batsman piling up runs in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests an opening batsman; it is the definition, a short word for an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an informal clipped word for the introductory opening section of a song or talk.

clue.text: Recorded fragment about endless wave

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: an end is a leftover scrap, as in a candle end
a roller is a long breaking wave, cut short by one letter

explanation.surface: A snippet of film or tape showing part of a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: END goes around the shortened wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to enter their name on a register or official list, so recorded fits the past participle.

clue.text: A scruff grabbing a good person’s foot

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: taken as written
the scruff of the neck is the nape
taken as written
a saint is a good person; ST is the abbreviation

explanation.surface: An urchin grabbing someone's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' seems physical but is metrical. The possessive on 'good person’s' is just surface glue; ST goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an anapaest is a metrical unit of two short syllables followed by a long one.

clue.text: Warmer in home — timers are reset

indicators.note: to reset is to set again differently, so the letters are placed in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Resetting the timers on the household heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but belongs in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An immersion heater is an electric element in a hot-water tank, common in British homes, that warms the water.

clue.text: Animal caught in field eaten by kitty

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it, enclosed on both sides
what is eaten ends up inside the eater

blocks.note: the pot or kitty is the pool of money in a card game
lea is a poetic word for a meadow
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A creature caught in a field and eaten by a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitty' pretends to be a cat but is the pool of stakes in a card game. There are two nested containers: the cricket letter inside the field, and both inside the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred European mammal of the weasel family, known for its smell.

clue.text: Fat friend, briefly ill, after doctor

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its last letter
one thing coming after another sets the order in which pieces are placed

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
MO is a medical officer
the word shortened by its final letter

explanation.surface: An overweight friend, briefly unwell, comes after a visit to the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like an adjective describing the friend; it is the noun definition. The shortened sickness follows the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm oil is an edible vegetable oil from oil-palm fruit, used as a cooking and food lipid.

clue.text: Sacrifice for me has to involve million dead

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: IMO, 'in my opinion', is texting shorthand for 'as far as I'm concerned'
M is the abbreviation for million
the late X is X who has died

explanation.surface: Someone asks what it would take to sacrifice a million dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for me' is the texting abbreviation for 'in my opinion', i.e. as far as I am concerned; 'late' meaning dead, as in 'the late king', supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as an offering, especially by burning, so it matches the verb sacrifice.

clue.text: Had unusually sound tips for purchase

indicators.note: done in an unusual way, so the letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
a noise is a sound

explanation.surface: Someone passing on shopping advice with unusual confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound tips for purchase' reads as buying advice; 'purchase' is the grip sense, and the synonym for 'sound' is mixed with HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or grip, and adhesion is the sticking that gives such traction.

clue.text: Tend to course around Seine’s banks

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
a river's banks are its edges, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: a run is a course or route
the first and last letters of the river's name

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to follow a route along the banks of the Seine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it turns the course word back to front before the river's edge letters follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to look after the sick, the caring verb sense of tend.

clue.text: Overtime pay for a barman, potentially?

definitions.text: Overtime pay for a barman, potentially?

blocks.note: surface reading: extra wages for someone serving drinks in a pub
setter's reading: a man of the Bar is a barrister, whose extra daily fee on a long-running case has a special name; a pub barman might also be called one who revives drinkers

explanation.walkthrough: A barrister is a member of the Bar, so 'barman' hides a lawyer. In English law a refresher is the extra daily fee paid to counsel when a trial runs on; 'potentially' flags that the word also fits someone serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal usage, a refresher is an additional fee paid to a barrister for each further day of a lengthy case.

clue.text: Putting in fortune, load a fleet

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it inside another thing

blocks.note: to fill is to load up
one's lot is one's fortune or fate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Investing a fortune to load up a fleet of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator comes first, so the piece named straight after it is the one that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats, the diminutive of Spanish flota.

clue.text: Stop sheep chasing the Alsatian?

indicators.note: one who chases follows behind, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: Alsace is in France, and le is French for 'the'
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: Calling off an Alsatian dog that is chasing sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alsatian is a German Shepherd dog, which fits the sheep, but here it means a person from Alsace, whose word for 'the' is French.
explanation.definitionFit: To let up is an idiom for easing off or ceasing, as rain lets up when it stops.

clue.text: Cat woman’s under pressure to detain soldier

indicators.note: in a down clue what is under something else is written below it
to detain is to hold, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
a soldier ant is a caste of ant that defends the colony
the possessive 'woman's' is 'her'

explanation.surface: A cat-woman under pressure to arrest a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' looks military but gives the insect, a crossword favourite. The two outer pieces hold it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a large wild cat, usually a leopard or a black-coated jaguar.

clue.text: Get on strike with upright character — rich sort?

blocks.note: to strike is to hit
the letter I is a single upright stroke
a toff is a posh, wealthy person in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a moral, upright rich person can get along with strikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright character' suggests an honest person; it is the letter shaped like a vertical line. A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit it off is an idiom for getting along well with someone from the first meeting.

clue.text: Brother’s style indeed shown after Mass

indicators.note: what is shown after comes later, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a ton is a unit of mass
'sure' as an exclamation means indeed, certainly

explanation.surface: A monk's way of life displayed after church Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' with its capital pretends to be the church service; it is weight. 'Brother' is a monk, and 'style' his haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of the head traditionally worn by monks, so it is a friar's haircut.

clue.text: See ark’s middle in river decorated with flowers

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
lo is an old word meaning look or see
the centre letter of the three-letter word

explanation.surface: Noah's ark, sailing on a river decked with blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a Cornish river, a crossword regular. The biblical exclamation 'lo' plus the ark's centre letter go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral describes things made of or patterned with blooms, as in a floral display.

clue.text: After time Austen novel brings complaint

indicators.note: coming after means following, so this piece is placed second
novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reading a Jane Austen novel after a while leads to someone grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Austen novel' calls up Emma or Persuasion; here 'novel' is an adjective meaning new, working on the author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, and complaint is a general word for an illness.

clue.text: Round[,] figure with right clothing is content

indicators.note: clothes wrap a body on every side, so the outer pieces enclose the inner one

blocks.note: ten is a number, a figure
O is round in shape
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A plump figure in the right clothes is happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like the adjective for happy, but it is the noun, the substance of something said or written.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of a speech or document is its general drift or gist, i.e. its substance.

clue.text: Shroud one round Conservative lying in state

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it
lying in a place means resting inside it

blocks.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Covering with a shroud a Conservative statesman lying in state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in state' evokes a funeral; 'state' is actually a US state abbreviation, holding everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To shroud is to wrap or veil something from view, so it is a synonym of hide.

clue.text: Fellow needing name for charming group

blocks.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a chap
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A man needing a name for his delightful band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charming' reads as delightful but means casting charms, i.e. spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering of witches, who cast charms, so the group is literally one that works spells.

clue.text: It was good to settle for a midday meal

definitions.text: It was good to settle for a midday meal

blocks.clueFragment: It was good to settle for a midday meal
blocks.note: surface reading: someone was happy to make do with a lunchtime snack

blocks.clueFragment: It was good to settle for a midday meal
blocks.note: setter's reading: a paper ticket that was valid ('good') as payment ('to settle') for a lunch, the past tense because the scheme has ended

explanation.walkthrough: 'good for' means valid for, and 'settle' means pay a bill. These were British meal tickets given by employers from the 1950s until the scheme ended in 2013, hence 'was'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticket was a paper token given by an employer, accepted by cafés as payment towards a lunchtime meal.

clue.text: Gold used by artist inspiring Golden Dawn

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA is a Royal Academician
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An artist mixing gold paint, inspired by the golden light of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden Dawn' reads as one phrase (also an occult society); split it, and the heraldic tincture goes inside the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the Latin name and goddess of the daybreak, used in English for the first light of morning.

clue.text: Form calculus takes where triangle replotted?

indicators.note: plotted again, i.e. redrawn in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A maths lesson where a triangle is redrawn on a graph in calculus.
explanation.walkthrough: The mathematical surface is apt: the area of a shape plotted on axes is found with one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: An integral is one of the two basic constructions of calculus, alongside the derivative, giving area under a curve.
